summary: Leviticus specifies one log of oil for the cleansing rite. A person who can afford fewer animals still brings the same amount of oil.

senses.definition: A unit of liquid capacity. In Leviticus it gives the quantity of oil presented with the guilt offering.

evidence.note: The list distinguishes the oil mixed into the flour from the additional log of oil.
The priest raises the lamb and the measured oil together.
The priest pours some of the oil from the log into his left palm.
The provision for a poor person still specifies a log of oil.
The priest raises the lamb and the log in this form of the rite as well.

evidence.locator: L00184 sense 2, Onkelos Lev 14:10 and Pesahim 109a

note: Leviticus gives no conversion into other units. The Ugaritic comparison establishes earlier use of the term for liquid capacity. The route by which the term spread is uncertain.
